# EQ-INSAR

> Lightweight, physics-based forward model for generating synthetic InSAR surface deformation data from earthquake sources. Designed for ML training, benchmarking, and sensitivity analysis.

EQ-INSAR is a Python package that generates synthetic Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) data for earthquake surface deformation. It uses the Davis (1986) point source model in an elastic half-space to compute 3D surface displacement, then projects it into satellite line-of-sight (LOS) geometry and converts to interferometric phase.

## Core Capabilities

- Generate single synthetic interferograms with configurable earthquake parameters (magnitude, strike, dip, rake, depth)
- Generate time series with pre-event, co-event, and post-event frames for ML training
- Batch generation with randomized parameters producing stacked (N, T, H, W) arrays
- Support for 9 SAR satellites: Sentinel-1, ALOS-2, TerraSAR-X, COSMO-SkyMed, RADARSAT-2, NISAR, SAOCOM, ENVISAT, ICEYE
- Export to GeoTIFF and NetCDF formats
- Core computation depends only on NumPy

## Installation

```
pip install eq-insar
```

## Quick Example

```python
from eq_insar import generate_synthetic_insar

result = generate_synthetic_insar(
    Mw=6.0,
    strike_deg=30, dip_deg=45, rake_deg=90,
    depth_km=10,
    satellite='sentinel1',
    orbit='ascending'
)
los_displacement = result['los_displacement']
wrapped_phase = result['wrapped_phase']
```

## Main API Functions

- `generate_synthetic_insar()` — Generate a single interferogram
- `generate_timeseries()` — Generate time series with pre/co/post-event frames
- `generate_training_batch()` — Batch generation with randomized parameters
- `batch_to_arrays()` — Convert batch to stacked NumPy arrays
- `sample_earthquake_parameters()` — Sample random earthquake parameters
- `get_satellite(name)` — Get satellite configuration
- `list_satellites()` — List all available satellites
- `davis_point_source()` — Compute displacement using Davis (1986) model
- `double_couple_moment_tensor()` — Create moment tensor from strike/dip/rake
- `compute_los_displacement()` — Project 3D displacement to LOS
- `save_geotiff()` / `save_netcdf()` — Export data

## Physics References

- Davis, P.M. (1986). Surface deformation due to a dipping hydrofracture. JGR.
- Aki, K. & Richards, P.G. (2002). Quantitative Seismology.
- Hanks, T.C. & Kanamori, H. (1979). A moment magnitude scale. JGR.
- Wells, D.L. & Coppersmith, K.J. (1994). Empirical relationships among magnitude, rupture length, rupture width, rupture area, and surface displacement. BSSA.
